source_text:
Τὴν ἁγίαν σύνοδον τῶν πατέρων τῶν ἐν Νικαίᾳ σύνοδον
ὄντως καθολικὴν καὶ ἀποστολικὴν γνωρίζομεν, καὶ πίστιν τὴν ἐκτεθεῖσαν ὑπὸ τῶν πατέρων τηνικαῦτα φυλάττομεν ἀκίνητον καὶ πρὸς τὸ διηνεκὲς ἀσπάρακτον μένειν εὔχομαι. Γέγονε δὲ τότε τοῖς πατράσιν ἀναγ καιότερον πλατύτερον ἐξηγήσασθαι περὶ τῆς δόξης τοῦ μονογε νοῦς, ἐπειδὴ τότε νεωστὶ φυομένην τὴν αἵρεσιν τοῦ Ἀρείου διὰ σπουδῆς ἔσχον ἐκκόψαι τὰ πρῶτα αὐτῆς προαναιροῦντες σπέρ ματα, πρὶν τελέως ἐκτραχυνθῆναι τὴν ἄκανθαν. Σεσιγημένου δὲ τηνικαῦτα τοῦ κατὰ τὸ πνεῦμα ζητήματος διὰ τοῦτο πλατύτερον μὲν οὐδὲν προσέθεσαν· τοῖς μέντοι γε συνετῶς ἀναγινώσκουσιν αὐτάρκης καὶ ἡ περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ πίστει διδασκα λία. Ὥσπερ εἰς πατέρα καὶ υἱὸν πιστεύειν, οὕτω καὶ εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα πιστεύειν ἐδογμάτισαν, μήτε ἑτέραν τινὰ φύσιν ἐπεισάγοντες τῇ θείᾳ καὶ μακαρίᾳ τριάδι μήτε τι τῶν ἐκ τῆς τριάδος ἀποτέμνοντες εἰς τὴν τῆς πίστεως ἔκθεσιν. Ἐπεὶ δὲ πρόσφατον ὁ σατανᾶς διασαλεύειν τὰς ἐκκλησίας ἐπιχειρῶν ἐνέβαλέ τισι περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος δισταγμόν, ἀναγκαῖον ἐπὶ τὴν πηγὴν ἀνατρέχειν τῆς πίστεως ἐξ ἧς καὶ οἱ κατὰ Νίκαιαν πατέρες ἀναρυσάμενοι τὴν ἔκθεσιν τῆς πίστεως ἐποίησαν. Τίς οὖν ἡμῶν ἡ τῆς πίστεως τελειότης;
thought_title: The Nicene faith is catholic and apostolic, and sufficient on the Spirit
orientation: Amphilochius, writing on behalf of a synod, is answering the recipients' inquiry about the faith by affirming the Nicene creed and explaining why the fathers said nothing more extensive about the Holy Spirit.
pass_a_gloss: The holy synod of the fathers, the synod in Nicaea, we recognize as truly catholic and apostolic, and the faith set forth by the fathers at that time we guard unmoved, and I pray that it remain unshaken forever. It became then more necessary for the fathers to explain more extensively about the glory of the only-begotten, since at that time the recently sprouting heresy of Arius they were eager to cut off, cutting away its first seeds beforehand, before the thorn became fully hardened. Since the question concerning the Spirit was then still silenced, for this reason they added nothing more extensive; yet for those who read intelligently the teaching about the Spirit in that faith is sufficient. Just as they decreed to believe in Father and Son, so also they decreed to believe in the Spirit, neither introducing any other nature into the divine and blessed Trinity nor cutting off any of the members of the Trinity in the exposition of the faith. But since recently Satan, attempting to shake the churches, cast into some a hesitation about the Spirit, it is necessary to run back to the source of the faith, from which also the fathers at Nicaea drew up and made the exposition of the faith. What then is the perfection of our faith?

choices.why: The adverb ὄντως modifies both adjectives, emphasizing the genuine character of the synod; 'catholic' and 'apostolic' are the standard creedal terms.

choices.term: ἀκίνητον καὶ πρὸς τὸ διηνεκὲς ἀσπάρακτον μένειν
choices.why: The two adjectives describe the faith's stability; πρὸς τὸ διηνεκές means 'for perpetuity,' rendered 'forever' to keep the temporal force.
rejected: fixed and unbroken for all time

choices.term: νεωστὶ φυομένην τὴν αἵρεσιν τοῦ Ἀρείου
choices.english: the recently sprouting heresy of Arius
choices.why: The participle φυομένην is present, emphasizing the heresy was just then growing; 'sprouting' preserves the botanical metaphor that continues with seeds and thorn.

choices.english: before the thorn became fully hardened
choices.why: The metaphor of the thorn (ἄκανθα) continues the agricultural imagery; ἐκτραχυνθῆναι means 'to become rough/hardened,' not 'to be uprooted.'
rejected: before the thorn was completely rooted out
before the thorn grew fully sharp

choices.term: Σεσιγημένου δὲ τηνικαῦτα τοῦ κατὰ τὸ πνεῦμα ζητήματος
choices.english: Since the question concerning the Spirit was then still silenced
choices.why: The perfect participle Σεσιγημένου has passive force ('having been silenced'), and τηνικαῦτα means 'at that time'; the genitive absolute gives the reason.
rejected: The question about the Spirit being silent then
Since the inquiry about the Spirit was quiet at that time

choices.term: ἐπὶ τὴν πηγὴν ἀνατρέχειν τῆς πίστεως
choices.english: to run back to the source of the faith
choices.why: ἀνατρέχειν means 'to run back up' to a source; πηγή is 'spring/source,' and the following relative clause identifies it as what the Nicene fathers drew from.
rejected: to return to the fountain of faith
to go up to the origin of the faith

pass_b_english: We recognize the holy synod of the fathers at Nicaea as truly catholic and apostolic, and we guard the faith set forth by the fathers at that time, praying that it may remain unmoved and unshaken forever. It became necessary then for the fathers to explain more fully the glory of the Only Begotten, because they were eager to cut off the recently sprouting heresy of Arius, cutting away its first seeds beforehand, before the thorn became fully hardened. But since the question concerning the Spirit was then still silenced, they added nothing more extensive about it. Yet for those who read intelligently, the teaching about the Spirit in that creed is sufficient. Just as they decreed belief in the Father and the Son, so also they decreed belief in the Spirit, neither introducing any other nature into the divine and blessed Trinity nor cutting off any member of the Trinity from the statement of faith. But since Satan, attempting afresh to shake the churches, has cast into some people doubt about the Spirit, it is necessary to run back to the source of the faith from which the fathers at Nicaea drew when they made their statement of faith. What, then, is the perfection of our faith?
